measurement.interval_order: GET then PUT; one then four flows
measurement.payload_validation: Every byte; receiver acknowledges upload count
measurement.cpu: Both LowTier processes; user plus system CPU
measurement.cpu_exclusions: Generator, service, SSH, and softirq work outside these processes
measurement.server_cpu_window: Includes control gaps and unloaded echo work
measurement.latency: Median of per-trial percentiles; linear interpolation for p95
measurement.wire: Unique TCP payload received; includes TLS, H2, and control traffic
measurement.wire_exclusions: Outer TCP/IP headers, outer ACKs, duplicate retransmissions, and most bulk-flow setup
measurement.missing_counter_policy: null means absent; an omitted ss field does not prove zero
measurement.bounded_producer: SO_SNDBUF request 32768; Linux reports 65536 per generator socket

limitations: Cohorts were sequential and not randomized.
Unbounded four-flow uploads encountered TCP memory pressure on jpaws.
The exact vendor-kernel path that first reduced send capacity remains unresolved.
Auto evaluates admission health and resources, rather than transfer speed or loaded latency.
H2 retains TCP head-of-line blocking and shared carrier failure.
Native scope excludes ordinary kernel TUN forwarding.

fleet.mode_source: Existing configurations retain the verified off default.
fleet.native_scope: Client-initiated direct TCP proxy flows to a userspace peer's own IPv4 address.
fleet.route_repair: btrouter: restored the default route declared by cmcc4 DHCP. Firewall and VPN rules are unchanged.
recovery: The live-switch fixture used startup overrides and was read-only. A complete TOML fixture restored writable control.
The fleet verifier lacked local reference files. Protected pre-install copies supplied those files.
The option verifier expected an explicit value. Schema verification confirmed the off default for unset values.
btrouter had no IPv4 default route. Restoring its declared DHCP route recovered authenticated peers and delivery.
fleet.limitations: Native H2 streams do not cover kernel TUN forwarding. Auto checks admission health and resources. It does not predict speed or loaded latency. Four-flow uploads showed kernel TCP memory pressure. The exact vendor shrink path remains unresolved. No artificial-loss trial was run. H2 retains TCP head-of-line blocking.
